channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US Lawmaker Plans to Challenge Trump's Reported Oil Deal with Russia
item.description: Republican Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick intends to challenge a reported agreement for the U.S. to purchase diesel fuel from Russia. He plans to introduce legislation, the 'Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act,' to force a House vote blocking Russian oil purchases, citing potential support from Democrats.

item.title: Afghanistan Ranks Third Globally in Unexploded Ordnance Deaths, UNAMA Warns
item.description: Afghanistan ranks third worldwide in fatalities from unexploded ordnance, with large areas contaminated by war remnants, UNAMA has warned. Children are particularly vulnerable, making up 80% of casualties, often from playing with explosive devices. UNAMA urges public awareness and reporting of suspicious objects to prevent further deaths and calls for sustained mine-clearance support.

item.title: Kazakhstan Meets Only 66% of Prosthetic and Orthopedic Aid Needs for People with Disabilities
item.description: Kazakhstan has met only 66.1% of the demand for prosthetic and orthopedic aid for people with disabilities as of October 1st. Overall, 80.6% of rehabilitation needs were met. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection reported a slight increase in fulfillment rates compared to the previous year, highlighting ongoing efforts to improve support.

item.title: Pakistan Army: 12 TTP and Afghan Taliban members killed in border areas
item.description: The Pakistan Army reported that 12 members of the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Afghan Taliban were killed in operations in border regions. The statement did not provide specific details on the timing or location of these operations.

item.title: Tajik Embassy in UK Invites Interested Individuals to Learn Tajik Language Online
item.description: The Tajik Embassy in London has announced an online Tajik language course for children of compatriots living in the UK and other interested individuals. Classes will be held twice a week. Interested parties must register by October 20, providing their name, age, and proficiency level.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 100 Afghan Migrant Families Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 104 families, totaling 448 people, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson for the Taliban, stated that these families entered through various border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak, Pul-e Abrisham, and Islam Qala.

item.title: Former Afghan President Karzai Urges Reopening of Schools and Universities to Girls
item.description: On the International Day of the Girl, former Afghan President Hamid Karzai called for schools and universities to reopen to girls. He stressed that empowering girls through access to education is crucial for Afghanistan's growth and development. Karzai urged society to prioritize girls' education, emphasizing its importance for the country's progress and the equal participation of women and girls.

item.title: Foreigner Detained for 15 Days in Almaty for Groping Woman in Park
item.description: A foreign national has been administratively detained for 15 days in Almaty for inappropriately touching a woman in Terrenkur Park. The individual, identified as a tourist who arrived in Kazakhstan the day before, was apprehended by local police. Authorities are reviewing his further stay in the country.

item.title: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport kills at least 12, injures hundreds
item.description: Yemeni Houthis launched a missile attack on Riyadh International Airport, killing at least 12 people and injuring approximately 400. This marks the third attack on the airport this week, and the most severe. Casualties included citizens from the US, Bangladesh, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt, in addition to Saudi nationals. The airport has temporarily closed.

item.title: FAO warns of increased rainfall and flood risks in Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) forecasts above-average rainfall in Afghanistan, potentially aiding rain-fed wheat cultivation but also increasing flash flood risks. Eastern, northeastern, northern, and central regions may see more rain in October, benefiting winter crops. However, intense rainfall could trigger floods and disrupt summer crop harvests. Rising fertilizer and seed prices, plus unfavorable market conditions, limit farmer investment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Houthi Attack on Saudi Arabian Capital's Airport
item.description: The Uzbek Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep sorrow and strongly condemned the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The strike resulted in at least 12 deaths and approximately 310 injuries, including citizens of Saudi Arabia and the US. Uzbekistan reaffirmed its support for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and security.

item.title: Police Open Criminal Case After Stampede at Kairat Nurtas Concert Injures Teenager
item.description: Police have opened a criminal case following a stampede at a Kairat Nurtas concert in Shymkent that critically injured an 18-year-old girl. Relatives reported the girl was trampled by the crowd. Organizers have been taken to the police, and the investigation is ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident.

item.title: Carbon Monoxide Detectors to Be Installed for Large Families in Kyzylorda Region
item.description: 150 carbon monoxide detectors will be installed in the homes of large families in difficult socio-economic situations in the Kyzylorda region. The devices, purchased with sponsorship, detect dangerous gas concentrations and alert residents. This initiative is part of preventive measures for the heating season to prevent fires and poisoning.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Attack on Riyadh International Airport, Calls for De-escalation
item.description: Uzbekistan has strongly condemned the attack on the international airport in Riyadh. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged an immediate cessation of such attacks, called for all parties to show restraint, and to prevent further escalation of tensions. The statement was released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New CIS Cooperation Strategy for Next 35 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has proposed a new strategy for the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) development until 2035, focusing on economic, infrastructure, and technological projects. President Tokayev suggested forming a portfolio of flagship industrial-technological projects and strengthening transport connectivity. Kazakhstan also advocates for expanding CIS international cooperation through a 'CIS Plus' format.

item.title: Houthis Warn Airlines to Avoid Saudi Airports After Deadly Riyadh Attack
item.description: Yemen's Houthi movement has warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, declaring them potential targets following a deadly attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. The warning excluded Mecca and Medina. Saudi authorities reported 12 fatalities, including citizens from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.

item.title: Houthis Attack Saudi Arabia's Capital Airport, Causing Casualties
item.description: The airport in Saudi Arabia's capital was attacked by Houthis, resulting in 12 fatalities and over 300 injuries. This incident follows claims by the Houthis of striking the airport. The General Authority of Civil Aviation temporarily suspended airport operations for damage assessment and security checks. Official Saudi sources indicated that missiles hit terminals three and four.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Airport Leaves 12 Dead, Over 300 Injured, State Media Reports
item.description: An attack by Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resulted in 12 deaths and 309 injuries, according to Egemen.kz. The report states the incident occurred days after the Houthis claimed responsibility for an airport strike. Saudi official sources cited by The Wall Street Journal indicated missiles hit terminals three and four, causing significant damage.

item.title: Millions of Afghan Girls Denied Education and Rights Under Taliban Rule on International Day of the Girl
item.description: On the International Day of the Girl, millions of girls in Afghanistan under Taliban rule are deprived of fundamental rights, particularly education. Over 2.4 million girls are barred from secondary education. Concerns about child marriage persist, with reports indicating around 30 percent of girls marry before 18. UN Women calls for global action to end child marriage.

item.title: Trump Agrees to Buy Russian Diesel After Criticizing Ukraine's Attacks on Oil Refineries
item.description: Donald Trump criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for attacks on Russian oil refineries, suggesting Ukraine needs a new leader capable of making peace. Trump stated he agreed to purchase diesel fuel from Russia after speaking with Vladimir Putin. Zelensky viewed this as enabling Russia's continued war efforts. US officials reportedly warned Ukraine to cease attacks on Russian refineries.

item.title: UNAMA Urges Taliban to End Discriminatory Practices Against Women
item.description: The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) has called on the Taliban to cease discriminatory treatment of women and girls. UNAMA stated that verbal abuse, beatings, and threats of arrest by Taliban officials violate fundamental rights, including freedom of movement and expression.

item.title: Yandex Services Experience Disruptions in Kazakhstan Following Drone Attacks
item.description: Yandex Go services, including taxi and food delivery, are experiencing disruptions in Kazakhstan. The company confirmed technical issues are affecting operations and is working on restoration, but timelines remain uncertain. Users report inability to book rides, impacting daily plans and courier work. Yandex cited distributed infrastructure for service operation.

item.title: Yandex Services Malfunction in Kazakhstan After Drone Attack on Data Centers
item.description: Following a drone attack on Yandex data centers in Russia, several Yandex services malfunctioned in Kazakhstan on Sunday, October 11. Yandex Go Kazakhstan confirmed technical issues causing temporary disruptions and apologized for the inconvenience. The company stated specialists are working to restore services as quickly as possible.

item.title: Yandex Services Cease Operations in Kazakhstan, Leaving Drivers and Couriers Unemployed
item.description: Yandex services, including taxi and delivery, have stopped working in Kazakhstan. This halt has left numerous drivers and couriers without work. The company has acknowledged the disruptions and is reportedly working on restoring services, but specific timelines for resumption remain unclear.

item.title: Indonesian Forest Fire Smoke Reaches Malaysia and Singapore
item.description: Smoke from forest fires on Indonesia's Sumatra and Kalimantan islands has reached Malaysia and Singapore. The dry weather caused by the El Niño phenomenon contributed to the fires. Several schools in Malaysia and Kuala Lumpur were closed due to poor air quality, affecting over 1.5 million students. Rescuers are also working to evacuate animals from the affected forest areas.

item.title: Yandex Go Services Temporarily Unavailable in Kazakhstan After Data Center Attack
item.description: Yandex Go services are temporarily unavailable in Kazakhstan following reports of an attack on the company's data center in Vladimir, Russia. Yandex Go stated that technical specialists are working to restore services as soon as possible. The company assured users that Kazakhstani users' personal data is stored securely within Kazakhstan, though global infrastructure may affect service availability.

item.title: Yandex Taxi and Courier Services Experience Outages Across Kazakhstan
item.description: Yandex taxi and courier services became unavailable in Kazakhstan on October 11. Users reported widespread issues with the app, citing a lack of available cars and significantly increased prices on alternative platforms. Some users speculated the outages could be related to cyberattacks targeting data centers.

item.title: Three Suspects Arrested in Almaty After Man Found Bagged and Removed from Apartment Building
item.description: Almaty police have arrested three suspects in connection with the disappearance of a man who was seen being carried out of his apartment building with a bag over his head. Neighbors reported suspicious activity prior to the incident, including the theft of mailbox keys and unauthorized entry into an apartment. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Innovation and Startup Project Parks to Support Entrepreneurs
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to create innovation and startup project parks to provide services for entrepreneurs. These parks will assist businesses in product manufacturing, commercializing scientific research, and accessing international markets. The initiative aims to foster technological development and economic growth within the country.

item.title: Taxation Changes Proposed: VAT, Simplified System, and Online Trade Regulations
item.description: Proposals are being made to increase the mandatory VAT registration threshold to 3 million somoni and introduce a 3% tax for online trade. These changes aim to adjust the current taxation system, including VAT and simplified tax regimes.

item.title: Piskent District Governor Accused of Pressuring Farmers; Farmers' Council Appeals to Prosecutor
item.description: An audio recording has surfaced showing the governor of Piskent district, Tashkent region, allegedly pressuring farmers and using abusive language. The incident occurred during a meeting about planting second crops on land cleared of wheat. Farmers claim the governor is threatening to seize land and obstruct wheat planting.

item.title: Pakistan Protests Demand Imran Khan's Release and End to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Military Operations
item.description: Supporters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) are protesting, demanding the release of Imran Khan and an end to military operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The chief minister stated he would not accept illegal actions like emergency rule. The federal government is considering imposing governor's rule or emergency measures amid counterterrorism policy disagreements.

item.title: US President Trump Criticizes Ukraine's Zelensky Over Russia Deal and Attacks
item.description: US President Donald Trump criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for attacking Russian oil refineries, stating it caused diesel prices to rise. Trump also accused Zelensky of not wanting to end the war and advised him to find a new leader capable of making deals. Washington had asked Kyiv to stop attacking refineries, but Zelensky proceeded.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Results in 12 Deaths and Over 300 Injuries
item.description: A Houthi attack on Riyadh has resulted in 12 fatalities and left over 300 people injured. The details of the attack and the extent of the damage are still emerging.

item.title: Uzbekistan Interior Ministry Reports on Crime Statistics and Fugitive Apprehensions
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Uzbekistan apprehended nearly 8,000 fugitives and reunited 4,863 missing persons with their families. The Interior Ministry reported a decrease in preventable crimes by 4,021 cases compared to the previous year. Youth, women, and unemployed citizens were involved in fewer crimes. Over 31,000 crimes were detected by law enforcement, including over 13,000 drug-related offenses.

item.title: Travelers Returning to Uzbekistan from Russia Warned of Bus Ticket Scammers
item.description: Scammers are exploiting the Uzautotrans service name to sell overpriced bus tickets and arrange illegal journeys from Russia to Uzbekistan. They use social media and YouTube to post fake ads, claiming tickets are unavailable at the counter and selling them at inflated prices. Passengers with fake tickets are often directed to unauthorized carriers. Travelers are urged to buy tickets only from official ticket offices or verified online platforms.

item.title: Riyadh Airport Operations Halted After Missile Strike Kills 12 and Injures Over 300
item.description: A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has killed 12 people and injured 309, with some in critical condition. The attack damaged terminals three and four, causing parts of the roof to collapse. Airport operations were temporarily suspended, and flights were canceled or rerouted. The incident occurred amid escalating conflict and military operations against Houthi rebels.

item.title: Houthi Missile Attack on Riyadh Airport Kills 12, Injures Over 300
item.description: A missile attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 8 and 10 resulted in 12 deaths and 309 injuries, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation. The Houthis claimed responsibility for launching two missiles. The attacks caused damage to airport facilities and a Saudi Arabian Airlines aircraft.

item.title: ISW: Russian Diesel Export Permit to Aid Moscow's War Financing
item.description: The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reports that allowing Russia to export diesel fuel will help Moscow finance its ongoing military operations. This measure is seen as a way for Russia to generate revenue to support its war efforts.

item.title: Andijan Region: Major Traffic Accident Claims Three Lives, Injures Four
item.description: A severe road traffic accident involving seven vehicles occurred in Buloqboshi district, Andijan region. Initial reports indicate a truck's brake failure led to a collision with multiple cars and damage to nearby shops. Three individuals died at the scene, and four were hospitalized with injuries.
